prerequisites: Dominion of certain mathematical and physical knowledge.

Prior completion of 'Resistencia de Materiales' (Strength of Materials), 'Elasticidad' (Elasticity), and 'Ampliación de Resistencia de Materiales' (Advanced Strength of Materials) with minimum proficiency.

learning_outcomes.text: Provide the tools to understand and analyze the resistant behavior of different structural systems.
Know the actions to consider in building, managing and interpreting current regulations.
Know the usual structural typologies in industrial constructions, as well as the simplifications and hypotheses used in calculation models.
Provide methods for analyzing bar structures to determine stress and deformation states, allowing verification of resistance and functionality requirements.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and their clear and succinct exposition.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to transmit concepts, ideas, processes, etc., related to Industrial Engineering orally and in writing, clearly and correctly.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for seeking sustainable engineering solutions.
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. BASIC CONCEPTS OF STRUCTURAL ANALYSIS: Concept of structure. Phases of structural calculation. Magnitudes in structural calculation. Relationships in structural calculation. Linearity and superposition of effects. Isostatic and hyperstatic structures. Strain energy.
Topic 2. TYPOLOGY OF STRUCTURES: Structural elements. Classification of structural elements. Classification of bar structural systems. Idealization of the most common elements in building.
Topic 3. STRUCTURAL SAFETY AND ACTIONS IN BUILDING.
Topic 4. ARTICULATED STRUCTURES: Introduction. Isostatic articulated structures. Displacement of nodes. Hyperstatic trusses.

Topic 5. LATTICE STRUCTURES: Introduction. Hypotheses and simplifications. Forces in bars and nodes. Force method and displacement method. Transformation of structures due to symmetries and anti-symmetries.

Topic 6. CALCULATION OF LATTICE STRUCTURES BY THE FORCE METHOD: Intratranslational structures with inextensible bars. Intratranslational structures with extensible bars. Translational structures. Force method applied to the calculation of continuous beams.

Topic 7. CALCULATION OF LATTICE STRUCTURES BY THE DISPLACEMENT METHOD: Introduction. Degree of freedom. Stiffness. Transmission coefficient. Approach to calculation in displacements. Intratranslational frames with inextensible bars. Structures with extensible bars.

Topic 8. MATRIX CALCULATION OF LATTICE STRUCTURES: Introduction. Local and global coordinates. Nomenclature. Stiffness matrix of a bar in local axes. Properties. Stiffness matrix of a bar in global axes. Rotation matrix. Stiffness matrix of the structure. Assembly. Load vector. Matrix equation of the structure. Calculation of node displacements in global axes. Calculation of reactions in global axes. Calculation of forces at the ends of bars in global axes. Calculation of forces at the ends of bars in local axes.
Classroom practicals, with problem development related to each topic covered in theoretical lectures.
Classes and/or seminars for practical exercise resolution.
assessment_rules: A minimum grade of 5 out of 10 is required in each of the assessment components to pass the course. Active participation in programmed activities, study supported by bibliography, using tutorials to resolve doubts, and systematic work on autonomous tasks are recommended.
